findings.summary: Rtskhiladze v. Mueller active as of 2025: DC Circuit reversed district court dismissal in August 2024, remanding retraction claim. District court issued opinion May 30 2025 granting/denying in part motion to dismiss; parties required to file joint status report by June 13 2025. Case terminated December 31 2025 per CourtListener. The Mueller footnote at issue states Rtskhiladze texted Cohen he 'stopped flow of some tapes from Russia' — the case is about defamation/retraction, not criminal liability.

EPA reconsideration timeline maps directly to Logical Strategies lobbying: Rtskhiladze hired Javelin Advisors in July 2025 (Q3 registration). On June 16 2025, EPA filed with Fifth Circuit to reconsider the chrysotile ban, seeking 30-month delay. On July 7 2025, EPA reversed course and withdrew the motion — shortly after public opposition. Rtskhiladze's Q4 2025 LDA report shows zero activity, consistent with lobbying objective collapsing after EPA withdrawal.

Rtskhiladze has longstanding personal and business relationships with Trump's inner circle. He brokered Trump Tower Batumi (Georgia) and discussed Trump Tower Moscow/Astana with Michael Cohen. He was cited in Mueller Report footnote regarding alleged Trump tapes (text: 'stopped flow of tapes from Russia'). His defamation suit (Rtskhiladze v. Mueller, Case 1:20-cv-01591) allowed to proceed by DC Circuit in Aug 2024. He donates to Trump PACs 'Never Surrender Inc' (Trump 2024 leadership PAC) and Trump National Committee JFC in 2025, from 32 Old Bethel Rd, Newtown CT.

Rtskhiladze's business portfolio spans Russia/Kazakhstan/Georgia energy and investment sectors with potential asbestos industry exposure. His Toroil Group conducts oil/energy deals in Russian Federation. His Silk Road Transatlantic Alliance is connected to Silk Road Group (Georgia), which was funded by BTA Bank Kazakhstan — the same jurisdiction as Kostanai Minerals, the world's largest chrysotile asbestos producer. Rtskhiladze's investments in the Former USSR energy sector, combined with 2025 active donations to Trump PACs while running Logical Strategies LLC's EPA asbestos lobbying campaign, establish a clear pattern: access-based lobbying leveraging pre-existing Trump relationships to influence a high-value regulatory outcome for a client with CIS/Former USSR connections.

Logical Strategies LLC paid Javelin Advisors (Sorial/Schiller/Seiden) $1.2M in Q3 2025 to lobby on EPA Asbestos Part 1 chrysotile rule (TSCA) and government contracts. Q4 2025 report shows no further activity — lobbying ceased after EPA withdrew its reconsideration motion in July 2025.

No FARA registration found for Rtskhiladze, Logical Strategies LLC, or Toroil Group in DOJ FARA database. Lobbying registered under LDA (domestic lobbying framework), not FARA (foreign agent framework). If Rtskhiladze is acting on behalf of foreign asbestos producers, the LDA filing would be legally insufficient — FARA exemption requires no foreign government or principal directing the work.

Rtskhiladze made at least $1,337.72 in 2025 political contributions to Trump-aligned committees: TRUMP NATIONAL COMMITTEE JFC INC ($468.46), WINRED ($468.46), NEVER SURRENDER INC ($262.86), RNC ($137.94). All contributions clustered February-May 2025, overlapping with the lobbying engagement. No employer or occupation listed on FEC records.

Uralasbest (Russia's largest chrysotile asbestos producer, 21% of global output) publicly praised Trump in 2018 with 'APPROVED BY DONALD TRUMP' on asbestos packaging. Kostanai Minerals (Kazakhstan, 20% global output) shared the post. Neither company has any detected FARA or LDA registrations in the US. The EPA chrysotile ban (March 2024) devastated these producers' US market access. Russia and Kazakhstan together represent ~68% of global chrysotile production.

OxyChem (Occidental Chemical) is the only US company that was still importing raw chrysotile asbestos as of 2023-2024, sourcing from Brazil and China (not Russia/Kazakhstan). Olin and Westlake had stopped importing by 2021 and 2016 respectively. The primary US beneficiaries of delaying the chrysotile ban are domestic chlor-alkali producers (OxyChem, Olin, Westlake), not Russian/Kazakh exporters directly — who lost US market access under the 2024 ban. Key question: who would specifically benefit from the EPA rule reconsideration if Rtskhiladze is the intermediary?

Toroil Group (Rtskhiladze as President) brokered oil/energy deals in Russia including advising on Russia's largest commercial wind farm. Rtskhiladze is also Managing Partner of Green Wind Energy Group Inc, working with US investment firms to develop wind farms in Former Soviet region. Silk Road Transatlantic Alliance (US subsidiary) brokered Trump Tower Batumi and explored Trump Tower Astana with Michael Cohen in 2011. BTA Bank Kazakhstan was 51% co-owner of Silk Road Bank Georgia until 2014. Silk Road Group acquired BTA's 49% in October 2014 — BTA Bank was embroiled in a massive fraud scandal under former chairman Mukhtar Ablyazov.

OpenSanctions search for 'Rtskhiladze' returns only Shalva Rtskhiladze (Georgian asset declaration dataset, ge_declarations), not Giorgi. No sanctions matches for Uralasbest or Kostanai Minerals. No EDGAR filings found for Uralasbest, Kostanai Minerals, Logical Strategies, or Rtskhiladze as SEC filers or named individuals. No active FARA registrations for Russia- or Kazakhstan-linked entities working on asbestos in the US.

curation.lead:
Giorgi Rtskhiladze is a Georgian-American businessman and author whose career spans Former Soviet energy brokerage, Trump-era real estate deal-making, and federal lobbying. As President of Toroil Group, he conducted oil and energy transactions in Russia [Finding #6391]. As co-owner of Silk Road Transatlantic Alliance — a US arm of Georgia's Silk Road Group, which at the time held a banking relationship with BTA Bank Kazakhstan — he brokered Trump Tower Batumi and discussed Trump Tower Moscow and Astana with Michael Cohen [Finding #6391]. A Mueller Report footnote recorded that Rtskhiladze texted Cohen that he had 'stopped flow of some tapes from Russia'; Rtskhiladze has contested that characterization in federal court since 2020 (Case 1:20-cv-01591), a lawsuit the DC Circuit permitted to proceed in August 2024 and that was terminated December 31, 2025 [Finding #6390].

In 2025, through his company Logical Strategies LLC, Rtskhiladze paid Javelin Advisors LLC — founded by former Trump Organization executive George Sorial and staffed by former White House official Keith Schiller — $1.2 million in Q3 2025 to lobby the EPA on the Part 1 chrysotile asbestos rule under TSCA and on government contracts [Finding #6384]. Lobbying was registered under the Lobbying Disclosure Act, not FARA; no FARA registration for Rtskhiladze, Logical Strategies, or Toroil Group was found in the DOJ database [Finding #6385]. During the same February–May 2025 period, Rtskhiladze made at least $1,337.72 in FEC-documented contributions to Trump-aligned committees including Never Surrender Inc, Trump National Committee JFC, and the RNC [Finding #6386].

The EPA chrysotile ban (March 2024) eliminated US market access for the two largest global producers: Uralasbest (Russia, 21% of global output) and Kostanai Minerals (Kazakhstan, 20%), together representing approximately 68% of world chrysotile production [Finding #6387]. Records show that the EPA filed in the Fifth Circuit on June 16, 2025 to seek a 30-month reconsideration of the ban, and on July 7, 2025, the agency withdrew that motion [Finding #6388]. Records indicate that Rtskhiladze's Q4 2025 Senate LDA report shows zero lobbying activity, a pattern consistent with the engagement ending after the EPA withdrawal [Finding #6388]. The identity of the ultimate client or clients directing the campaign has not been established in the public record.
curation.system_role: Giorgi Rtskhiladze is a Georgian-American businessman who has operated across Former Soviet energy markets, Trump-era real estate development in the Caucasus, and federal lobbying on EPA asbestos regulation through former Trump White House personnel.

sections.title: EPA Asbestos Lobbying Campaign
sections.content:
Logical Strategies LLC — of which Rtskhiladze is the founding partner — retained Javelin Advisors LLC in Q3 2025, paying $1.2 million to lobby on the EPA Part 1 chrysotile asbestos rule under the Toxic Substances Control Act and on government contracts [Finding #6384]. George Sorial, a Javelin co-founder and former Trump Organization executive, and Keith Schiller, a Javelin lobbyist whose covered position was Deputy Assistant to President Trump and Director of Oval Office Operations, were the registered lobbyists [Connection #3234][Connection #3235].

The timeline of EPA action maps against the lobbying engagement. Records show that the EPA filed in the Fifth Circuit on June 16, 2025 seeking a 30-month reconsideration of the March 2024 chrysotile ban [Finding #6388]. Records indicate that on July 7, 2025, EPA withdrew that motion following public opposition [Finding #6388]. Records indicate that Rtskhiladze's Q4 2025 LDA report records zero activity, and Javelin filed no lobbying disclosures on this matter after the withdrawal [Finding #6388]. The engagement lasted approximately one quarter. The LDA framework does not require disclosure of the ultimate client if Logical Strategies is acting as the registrant principal; FARA, by contrast, would require disclosure if a foreign government or foreign principal were directing the work [Finding #6385]. No FARA registration for Rtskhiladze, Logical Strategies, or Toroil Group appeared in the DOJ FARA database as of the research date [Finding #6385].

Rtskhiladze's FEC-documented political contributions during February–May 2025 total at least $1,337.72, distributed across Never Surrender Inc ($262.86), Trump National Committee JFC Inc ($468.46), WinRed ($468.46), and the RNC ($137.94) [Finding #6386]. All contributions are clustered in the period overlapping with the Q3 2025 LDA registration [Finding #6386]. No employer or occupation is listed on the FEC records [Finding #6386].

sections.title: Chrysotile Market and the Question of Beneficial Interest
sections.content:
The March 2024 EPA rule banning chrysotile asbestos was the regulatory event that the Javelin engagement targeted [Finding #6384]. Uralasbest, Russia's largest chrysotile producer at approximately 21% of global output, had publicly circulated packaging bearing the phrase 'APPROVED BY DONALD TRUMP' in 2018; Kostanai Minerals of Kazakhstan, at approximately 20% of global output, amplified the post [Finding #6387]. Neither Uralasbest nor Kostanai Minerals has any detected FARA or LDA registrations in the United States [Finding #6392]. Russia and Kazakhstan together account for an estimated 68% of global chrysotile production [Finding #6387]. No EDGAR filings were found for Uralasbest, Kostanai Minerals, Logical Strategies, or Rtskhiladze as SEC filers or named individuals [Finding #6392].

The direct US importers present a different picture. According to trade records, OxyChem (Occidental Chemical) was the only US company still importing raw chrysotile as of 2023–2024, sourcing from Brazil and China rather than Russia or Kazakhstan [Finding #6389]. According to the same records, Olin ceased importing by 2021 and Westlake by 2016 [Finding #6389]. Analysis of import data indicates that the primary US beneficiaries of delaying the ban are domestic chlor-alkali producers — OxyChem, Olin, Westlake — not Russian or Kazakh exporters, who had already lost US market access under the 2024 rule [Finding #6389]. Analysis of the same data indicates that if the Brazil-source supply were also restricted, Russian and Kazakh producers would be the next available global source [Finding #6389]. The identity of any party directing or funding the Logical Strategies campaign has not been established in the public record; the available evidence does not resolve whether the beneficial interest is domestic (chlor-alkali industry), foreign (CIS producers seeking future US market re-entry), or both.

sections.title: Trump Network Relationships and the Mueller Report Citation
sections.content:
Rtskhiladze's business relationship with Trump's circle predates the 2025 lobbying engagement by over a decade. Through Silk Road Transatlantic Alliance, he brokered Trump Tower Batumi and explored Trump Tower Astana and Moscow with Michael Cohen in 2011 [Finding #6364]. Silk Road Transatlantic Alliance is a US subsidiary of Silk Road Group SA (Georgia); BTA Bank Kazakhstan held a 51% co-ownership stake in Silk Road Bank Georgia until Silk Road Group acquired the remaining 49% in October 2014 [Finding #6391]. BTA Bank had at that point been the subject of a major fraud proceeding involving former chairman Mukhtar Ablyazov [Finding #6391].

The Mueller Report cited Rtskhiladze in a footnote recording that he texted Cohen that he had 'stopped flow of some tapes from Russia' [Finding #6390]. Rtskhiladze filed suit in 2020 (Case 1:20-cv-01591, Rtskhiladze v. Mueller) seeking retraction of that characterization [Finding #6390]. The DC Circuit reversed a district court dismissal in August 2024 and remanded the retraction claim; the district court issued a partial grant/denial on a motion to dismiss on May 30, 2025 [Finding #6390]. The case was terminated December 31, 2025 per CourtListener [Finding #6390]. The litigation is a defamation and retraction action; it does not constitute a finding of criminal liability [Finding #6390].

Rtskhiladze is listed on LinkedIn as the founder of Logical Strategies LLC (New York) and as Managing Partner of Green Wind Energy Group Inc, a vehicle for US investment firm partnerships in wind farm development in the Former Soviet region [Finding #6391]. He is also the author of Kompromat: My Story from Trump to Mueller and USSR to USA [Finding #6364]. His 2025 political contributions are documented from 32 Old Bethel Rd, Newtown CT 06470 [Finding #6386].

sections.title: Former Soviet Business Network and Financial Relationships
sections.content:
Toroil Group, with Rtskhiladze as President, brokered oil and energy transactions in Russia and provided advisory services including work on Russia's largest commercial wind farm [Finding #6391]. Green Wind Energy Group Inc, where Rtskhiladze is Managing Partner, pursues wind farm development in the Former Soviet region in partnership with US investment firms [Finding #6391]. These roles establish an active operational footprint in Russian energy markets concurrent with his US lobbying activities.

Cross-reference of Rtskhiladze's CIS energy relationships, the Silk Road Group–BTA Bank Kazakhstan connection, and his 2025 lobbying on behalf of a party with undisclosed identity indicates a pattern consistent with leveraging pre-existing Trump relationships to serve CIS-connected interests; this is a synthesis finding rated medium confidence [Finding #6366]. No direct documented link between Rtskhiladze and Uralasbest or Kostanai Minerals was identified during the research period [Finding #6392]. No OpenSanctions entry exists for Giorgi Rtskhiladze; only Shalva Rtskhiladze appears, in Georgia's asset declaration dataset [Finding #6392].

open_questions: Who is the beneficial client directing the Logical Strategies LLC lobbying campaign — specifically, does the engagement originate with a domestic chlor-alkali producer (OxyChem, Olin, Westlake), a CIS chrysotile producer, or a third party not yet identified?

Does Toroil Group have any documented commercial relationship with Uralasbest, Kostanai Minerals, or any other CIS chrysotile producer that would indicate the lobbying campaign served those companies' interests?
What is the full text of the Rtskhiladze v. Mueller settlement or terminal order, and did the resolution include any agreed statement of facts regarding the Mueller Report footnote characterization?
Is there a retainer agreement, engagement letter, or sub-client disclosure in any Senate LDA or House LD-2 filing identifying the ultimate party for whom Logical Strategies engaged Javelin Advisors?

What is the current operational status of Silk Road Transatlantic Alliance, and does it maintain any financial or contractual relationship with entities connected to BTA Bank or its successor structures in Kazakhstan?
